guides.title: Structural chart reading
guides.concept: A trend is a sequence of observable swing relationships, not a guarantee that the next swing will continue.
guides.procedure: Mark two consecutive observable swing highs and lows; explain whether each exceeds or undercuts the preceding swing.
guides.limit: A breakout over a level is a hypothesis about continuation, not proof of buying intent.
guides.invalidation: The next observed swing invalidates the proposed structure, or the chart lacks enough visible pivots.
guides.commonError: Treating a single green candle as confirmed trend structure.

guides.title: Candles and price information
guides.concept: A candle summarizes OHLC observations for one interval; it does not encode the sequence between the high and low.
guides.procedure: Identify body, upper/lower wicks, open, close and total range on a completed candle.
guides.limit: A large upper wick can be consistent with rejection, but cannot prove who sold or why.
guides.invalidation: A wick interpretation conflicts with the broader visible series or an unseen candle is required.
guides.commonError: Assuming the candle's high occurred after its low without tape evidence.

guides.title: VWAP as context
guides.concept: Volume-weighted average price summarizes a defined set of trades, not a standalone trading instruction.
guides.procedure: Describe where the currently displayed price is relative to the properly scoped VWAP.
guides.limit: Price above VWAP does not prove the next trade will be profitable.
guides.invalidation: The comparison depends on missing trade/volume inputs or a different session boundary.
guides.commonError: Describing a two-print weighted mean as verified full-session VWAP.

guides.title: EMA and trend context
guides.concept: An exponential moving average weights recent completed closes more heavily; it is a lagging statistic.
guides.procedure: Identify the indicator period and whether its inputs stop at the current revealed bar.
guides.limit: A cross of two moving averages does not guarantee continuation.
guides.invalidation: The input history or EMA calculation boundary cannot be verified.
guides.commonError: Calculating an EMA with future closes or presenting a cross as a fill signal.

guides.title: Volume and participation
guides.concept: Volume counts reported units over a defined interval; volume alone does not reveal who initiated each trade.
guides.procedure: Compare observed volume with the same-length interval of a defensible reference sample.
guides.limit: Large volume is consistent with activity, not proof of a specific participant's motive.
guides.invalidation: Reference-session times, corporate actions or reported volume units are inconsistent.
guides.commonError: Comparing a full-day volume bar with a one-minute bar.

guides.title: Multi-timeframe alignment
guides.concept: Higher and lower timeframes are different aggregations of the same chronology, not independent confirmations.
guides.procedure: State the close of each visible aggregation before describing alignment.
guides.limit: A lower-timeframe reaction can occur inside an unresolved higher-timeframe candle.
guides.invalidation: The higher-timeframe candle is unfinished at the decision timestamp.
guides.commonError: Using the finished higher-timeframe bar to justify an earlier entry.

guides.title: Breakout observation
guides.concept: A breakout is an observed move beyond a previously identified level, not a promise of follow-through.
guides.procedure: Define the level using older visible bars, then note current price/volume behavior.
guides.limit: Crossing the level briefly may be a failed move; a break alone cannot prove demand.
guides.invalidation: Price returns beneath the level under the predetermined invalidation rule.
guides.commonError: Moving the breakout level after seeing later candles.

guides.title: Failed-breakout analysis
guides.concept: A failed breakout occurs when price cannot sustain the specified break within the chosen observation window.
guides.procedure: Document the original level and rule for recognizing a failure before revealing later bars.
guides.limit: A return to the range is an observation, not proof that every subsequent candle must decline.
guides.invalidation: The observation window ends without the required return below the break.
guides.commonError: Calling every intrabar pullback a confirmed failed breakout.

guides.procedure: Mark the existing trend, countertrend segment, and proposed invalidation point.
guides.limit: A pullback can deepen into a reversal; the label is provisional.
guides.invalidation: The reference trend no longer meets the previously written structural criteria.

guides.limit: The level describes prior extremes, not an executable order price.
guides.invalidation: Session mapping or corporate-action adjustment is unavailable or inconsistent.

guides.title: Risk per share
guides.concept: Planned risk per share is the absolute difference between entry assumption and predefined stop.
guides.procedure: Compute distance before choosing size; note fees and gap risk separately.
guides.limit: A stop order does not guarantee a loss capped at that amount.
guides.invalidation: Stop distance is zero, not observable, or based on future information.
guides.commonError: Multiplying expected reward by shares and calling it maximum risk.

guides.title: Share-count mathematics
guides.concept: The basic whole-share ceiling is floor(risk budget / planned per-share loss).
guides.procedure: Calculate budget, stop distance and maximum whole shares, then check liquidity and buying-power limits.
guides.limit: The calculated size is not a guarantee that a stop will fill at its level.
guides.invalidation: The trade exceeds buying power, liquidity assumptions, or the predetermined loss budget.
guides.commonError: Rounding quantity upward beyond the planned risk budget.

guides.title: Risk/reward planning
guides.concept: Planned reward-to-risk is prospective distance to a target divided by prospective stop distance.
guides.procedure: Document proposed entry, stop and target before using future data.
guides.limit: A large hypothetical ratio does not establish execution odds or win rate.
guides.invalidation: A nonpositive stop distance or target on the wrong side invalidates the setup.
guides.commonError: Treating a stated target as a realized profit.
